subject: Brightpath quickstart & deployment fit — sandbox access and rate profile
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brightpath quickstart & deployment fit — sandbox access and rate profile

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum:

What I heard — Brightpath wants:
- Evaluate hosted API first (fastest path) to validate accuracy and latency on your summarization model pipeline.
- Primary concern is PII handling and production residency (may require Dedicated/VPC later).
- Need to validate both sustained throughput and short bursts (peak 400 rps in peak minutes; typical steady-state ~60 rps).

Our suggested evaluation flow (fast, low-friction):
1) Sandbox access: we’ll provision a temporary hosted API sandbox (credentials + isolated project).
2) Endpoint mapping: two endpoints — a low-latency streaming endpoint for interactive summaries and a batch endpoint for nightly bulk jobs.
3) Rate slice: we’ll configure a rate window that simulates your traffic (we can set to 100 rps initially, ramp to 400 rps for short windows).
4) Data handling: for the sandbox we’ll enable redaction tooling and a short retention policy; Marissa will share the security checklist items you can use for compliance review.

Attachments I’m including (stubs):
- Brightpath_scope_estimate_v1.pdf (proposal + estimated trial capacity)
- trial-endpoint-slice.csv (sample traffic slices to use in load tests)

Ask from you:
- Confirm you want the hosted sandbox (yes/no) and an approximate date to start tests next week.
- Any additional stakeholders to cc (security, procurement)?

If hosted evaluation shows good latency/quality and residency is acceptable, we’ll outline the Dedicated/VPC path (timelines and cost delta). If not, we’ll scope a Private deployment evaluation.

I’ll also schedule a short 30-minute session with one of our solutions engineers (Marissa recommended) to walk your infra team through the sandbox and the load test plan.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

---
Note: If you want an NDA in place before we share the sandbox credentials, tell me and I’ll loop in Legal.

From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@brightpath.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Brightpath quickstart & deployment fit — sandbox access and rate profile

Thanks, Jonas — great summary. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) We’re happy to start with hosted sandbox but need to validate that logs/inputs containing customer PII are not retained longer than 7 days during the trial. Can you confirm retention controls for sandbox projects?

2) The 400 rps peak is an intermittent spike when our webhooks batch during month-end. For the evaluation we can emulate a 5-minute spike to 400 rps; steady-state for the demo will be closer to ~50–80 rps.

3) Two internal folks to loop in:
- Priya Natarajan (security@brightpath.ai) — she’ll vet the security checklist.
- Mark Chen (infra@brightpath.ai) — will own the load test exec.

4) Curious about rate limiting behavior — e.g., do you return 429s on per-endpoint concurrency exceed, or do you queue?

If you can confirm retention + rate behavior I’ll greenlight the sandbox start next Tuesday (28 Sep).

Thanks,
Alicia Moreno
Head of Product — Brightpath Analytics
alicia@brightpath.ai

On Wed, 22 Sep 2026 at 08:04, Alicia Moreno <alicia@brightpath.ai> wrote:
> Adding Priya and Mark for visibility.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <security@brightpath.ai>, Mark Chen <infra@brightpath.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Brightpath quickstart & deployment fit — sandbox access and rate profile

Hi Alicia / Priya / Mark —

Thanks — answering point-by-point and proposing next steps:

Retention & PII handling:
- Sandbox retention: default 7 days for request/response payloads in the evaluation sandbox (we can shorten to 24 hours if you prefer). No persistent storage outside the sandbox project will be used.
- Redaction: we can enable automatic redaction hooks for common PII patterns (SSNs, emails, credit card numbers) during ingestion.
- Logs: audit events (that do not include raw payloads) are retained for 30 days in control plane; we can provide a redacted audit export for your security review.

Rate limiting behavior:
- Hosted evaluation endpoints enforce two controls: per-project request rate and per-token rate.
- On hitting the configured window, the system returns 429s for excess requests (we do not queue indefinitely in the public hosted plan).
- For the sandbox we can enable a short burst queue (30s) so your 5-minute spike can be absorbed with staged throttling rather than immediate 429s. That will let you validate graceful degradation.

Proposed immediate next steps (to start Tuesday 2026-09-28):
1) I’ll send sandbox creds and a short-runbook by end of day today.
2) Marissa (cc’d) will run a 30-minute onboarding with your infra team on Tuesday 09:30 PT to walk endpoints, keys, and traffic slices.
3) We’ll provision a trial rate window: steady 80 rps with scheduled 5-minute spike to 400 rps; adjust token caps to match your average payload size (please share average tokens per request — Mark?).
4) I’ll share the scoped estimate PDF and the trial-endpoint-slice.csv (attached) — if procurement needs a simple statement of work for the sandbox we can convert the attached into that doc.

If that sounds good I’ll kick off the sandbox provisioning now.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Brightpath running.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: Brightpath_scope_estimate_v1.pdf (pdf), trial-endpoint-slice.csv (csv)
